CLARA v0.1 · A learning sandbox for operational dependencies. Synthetic people, rooms and timings. No AI predictions or clinical decision-making.
CONCEPT & PROVENANCE

From tracking to understanding flow.

This prototype is grounded in the supplied “30 min with Matt (Melinda Yormick)” meeting notes, October 19, 2026, and five CLARA technology slide images. The notes are Gemini-generated and may contain transcription errors.

What comes from the source material

The meeting describes UWB location sensing, a hospital world model spanning pre-op, ORs and recovery, and operational events linking people and equipment (00:01:20–00:03:25; 00:40:48–00:42:09). It separates deterministic orchestration from a possible learning layer (00:52:53–00:55:38). The slides describe event → sense → notify → act → learn, and illustrate an ultrasound conflict in “Everyday Workflows & Critical Moments.”

What this prototype invents

Three ORs, six cases A–F, synthetic patients P-A–P-F, three dedicated teams, one shared ultrasound, all schedules and durations, staff office/workroom/lounge routines, corridor routes, and this floor layout. These are teaching assumptions, not pilot data or validated hospital workflow.

  • Day begins at 08:00. Patients arrive 15 minutes before their planned start (clamped to 08:00).
  • Case A: 45 minutes, ultrasound first 15. B: 40 minutes, ultrasound first 20. C: 35 minutes, ultrasound first 20. Extra hold extends both A’s equipment use and case duration.
  • D, E and F last 35 minutes. Each waits for its room’s previous case, 15-minute turnover and dedicated team. Teams are dedicated to their OR but move between cases. Surgeons visit the staff office. Nurses remain in the OR for 10 minutes of room duties, then visit the nurse workroom. Anesthesia staff walk to recovery, stay 3 minutes for handoff, then visit the lounge. Staff return by the later of their next planned start or the end of 15-minute room turnover. Each staff trip takes 2 minutes. Team 1 and US-01 are already positioned in OR 1 at 08:00. These routines are illustrative, not hospital policy. No cross-room staffing is modeled.
  • Ultrasound turnaround is 3 minutes cleaning at the previous OR plus 2 minutes of corridor travel directly to the next booked OR (A → B → C), then back to the equipment hub after C. It remains unavailable until arrival. Case starts require the assigned team and required ultrasound to be physically in the OR.
  • Recovery lasts 30 minutes with unconstrained capacity. Pre-op capacity is also unconstrained. Patient transfers are instantaneous. Cleaning is a time gate, not sterilization validation. No clinical readiness, emergencies, sensing uncertainty or manual interventions are modeled.
  • Playback is deterministic discrete-event replay. Equal-time completions precede arrivals and requests; remaining ties use stable insertion order; no randomness, learning, recommendations or notifications are implemented.

Staff activity between cases varies by role and hospital. AORN’s discussion of room turnover provides general workflow context; it does not prescribe or validate this prototype’s destinations or timings.

The deck’s prediction and savings statements describe its product vision. This prototype does not test or reproduce those claims. Its readiness rules are software resource gates only.
